date.year: svādadigābhūta (corrupt chronogram; possibly 546 or 586, see notes)
date.nakshatra_yoga: Śobhana yoga; nakṣatra possibly Puṣya (pujā(rkka) = puṣyārka?)

purpose: Copied from an earlier exemplar (pūrvādarśadarśanena); the learned are asked to correct it (baudhe śodhanīyaṃ).
notes: The cataloguer marks the chronogram as corrupt (†). svāda (taste) = rasa = 6, bhūta (element) = 5, and dig (direction) is normally 10, but here it must be a single digit, so 4 or 8. Read right to left this gives NS 546 (CE 1425/26) or NS 586 (CE 1465/66). Both fit the cataloguer's guess of the 15th century, but neither is certain. The era is not stated; NS is presumed for a Newari-script copy by a Kāyastha. 'pujā(rkka)' probably stands for puṣyārka, i.e. Puṣya nakṣatra on a Sunday; Puṣya on Phālguna śukla 12 is astronomically plausible. Śobhana is the yoga. The toponym 'śrīdavāraṇima' (catalogue: 'Khāraṇima???') is uncertain; it is given as the scribe's residence (adhivāsinā), not explicitly as the place of copying. '(a ‥na)' after the name is a lacuna, perhaps ātmanā. The scribe's name is clear; the place name and date are doubtful.
